Methods for zinbreg objects

Source: R/methods-zinbreg.R
zinbreg-methods.Rd

Standard S3 methods for fitted zero-inflated negative binomial models returned by zinbreg(). Coefficient names follow pscl::zeroinfl(): count_* for the count model and zero_* for the zero-inflation model.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
coef(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
vcov(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "pearson"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  type = c("response", "count", "zero", "prob"),
  at = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x, object

A fitted "zinbreg" object (or, for print.summary.zinbreg(), a "summary.zinbreg" object).

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Further arguments (ignored).

model

For coef() and vcov(): "full" (both parts), "count", or "zero".

type

For residuals(): "response" (y - (1 - pi) mu) or "pearson" (response residual divided by sqrt((1 - pi) mu (1 + pi mu + mu / theta))). For predict(): "response" ((1 - pi) mu, the mean of Y), "count" (mu, the mean of the NB component), "zero" (pi, the probability of a structural zero), or "prob" (a matrix of P(Y = k) for k in at).

newdata

Optional data frame for prediction. If omitted, the original data are used.

at

For type = "prob": the counts at which to evaluate probabilities (default 0:max(y)).

Value

summary() returns an object of class "summary.zinbreg" with coefficient tables (estimates, standard errors, z values, p-values) for the count part (including Log(theta)) and the zero part. logLik() returns a "logLik" object with a df attribute (all coefficients plus one for theta), so AIC() and BIC() work.

Examples

data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
fit <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + kid5 + ment | ment, data = bioChemists)
coef(fit, model = "zero")
#> (Intercept)        ment 
#>  -0.7949061  -0.6193810 
sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))
#> count_(Intercept)    count_femWomen        count_kid5        count_ment 
#>       0.071295206       0.071503972       0.047968403       0.003456912 
#>  zero_(Intercept)         zero_ment 
#>       0.350163301       0.249061969 
AIC(fit)
#> [1] 3123.505
nd <- data.frame(fem = "Women", kid5 = 0, ment = c(0, 10, 30))
predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "zero")
#>            1            2            3 
#> 3.111162e-01 9.213803e-04 3.845603e-09 
predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "response")
#>         1         2         3 
#> 0.8988515 1.6630515 2.7091566 
# expected number of zeros
sum(predict(fit, type = "prob", at = 0))
#> [1] 286.3748
